answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying influence to a costly reputation bond, not to identity count. Each agent locks a stake and earns trust only through verified, useful work over time; a single cipher key signs all its actions, so reputation cannot be copied to clones without also splitting stake and history. Like a mesa rising above a flat nebula of cheap identities, a trusted agent stands out only after sustained effort. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must fund thousands of stakes and histories, and risk slashing for fraud, making forgery costlier than any gain.
